name: Chicken Alfredo Lasagna

ingredients.item: Frozen Lightly Breaded Chicken Breast Bites
ingredients.buy: 2 lb 5 oz, baked from frozen and roughly chopped
a generous pinch of each (about 1 1/2 tsp salt and 3/4 tsp black pepper)

writer_notes: All 8 bought ingredients are used by a step: chicken (bake/chop), cottage cheese + alfredo + salt + pepper (blend), noodles + mozzarella + parmesan + parsley (assemble/garnish). No orphaned ingredients and no step uses anything the list does not buy.
Per-serving macros from locked view: 496 cal, 40.7 g protein, 34.4 g carbs, 21.4 g fat. Band cal 450-800 and protein >= 40 both met; noodles supply the required real carb source.

Scaling flag (consistent ~2.33x source, looks correct for 14 servings): chicken 1 lb -> 2 lb 5 oz; cottage cheese 2 cups -> 4 2/3 cups; alfredo 3/4 cup -> 1 3/4 cups; mozzarella 8 oz -> 18.5 oz; parmesan 4 oz -> 9 1/3 oz; noodles 9 sheets -> 21 sheets.

Protein-source flag: run condition names boneless skinless chicken breast; the build uses FROZEN LIGHTLY BREADED chicken breast bites (breast meat, but breaded). Macros still pass the band. Flagged for the gate in case plain unbreaded breast is required.

No cost figures were in the locked view and no cost_lines were provided, so cost_closing uses the ${{cost_ps}} token and per-serving macros use {{cal}}/{{protein}} tokens. No per-package or per-ounce savings claims were made because none could be traced.
Parsley is used only on the first two layers per the source; the top finishes with mozzarella and parmesan only. Reflected in make_it and steps.
No em dashes or en dashes used anywhere; only plain hyphens in compound words.

prose.intro_html: Here is the thing about lasagna. It usually shows up loaded with cream, sausage, and a carb bill that quietly undoes a whole week of good choices. This one does not. We bake up frozen breaded chicken breast bites, blend low fat cottage cheese right into the alfredo so the whole tray turns creamy without a river of heavy cream, and layer it all with fresh mozzarella, parmesan, and no-boil noodles. What comes out of the oven is honest comfort food that lands at {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein per serving. Fourteen containers of Sunday dinner, waiting to be reheated on a Tuesday when you have nothing left in the tank.
prose.shop_smart: Let me walk you through the cart so you buy it right the first time. The star is a bag of frozen lightly breaded chicken breast bites, and you want a little over two pounds of them; they go in the oven straight from frozen, so no thawing to plan around. Cottage cheese does the heavy lifting on the creamy layer, so grab a large tub of the low fat kind, right around two pounds five ounces worth. One jar of alfredo sauce covers the one and three quarter cups the recipe asks for, and a roasted garlic version earns its shelf space here. For the melt, pick up fresh mozzarella and a wedge of parmesan you grate yourself, since it melts cleaner than the pre-shredded stuff. No-boil noodles are the whole point, so you can skip dragging out a boiling pot; you will lay down twenty one sheets, so check the count on the box and buy enough to cover that before you leave the aisle. A bunch of fresh parsley finishes it, and the salt and pepper you already own.
prose.make_it:
Start by heating your oven to 425 degrees. Bake or air fry the frozen chicken bites straight from frozen, right off the package instructions, then roughly chop them into bite size pieces once they are cooked through. While that is going, blend the cottage cheese, the alfredo sauce, and a pinch of salt and pepper together until it is smooth. That blended cottage cheese is your secret weapon; it carries the creamy alfredo flavor and stacks the protein without a drop of heavy cream.

Now build it. Coat the bottom of your baking dish with a thin layer of that sauce, lay down three noodle sheets, then add another layer of sauce, the chopped chicken, a scatter of parsley, mozzarella, and parmesan. Repeat the layers the same way, but only use parsley on the first two layers, and finish the very top with just mozzarella and parmesan. Cover the dish and bake for thirty minutes, then uncover it and give it another ten to fifteen minutes, until the cheese is bubbly and browning around the edges. Garnish with a little fresh parsley and grated parmesan, and let the whole thing rest at least five minutes before you slice. That rest is not optional if you want squares that hold together instead of a puddle.
prose.portion_html: Here is where your containers earn their keep, and where I need you to not eyeball it. Once the lasagna has rested, set your baking dish on a kitchen scale, subtract the weight of the empty dish if you know it, and divide what is left by fourteen. That number is your target weight per container. Portion by the scale, not by the knife, and every single one of your fourteen meals lands at the same {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein. Cut squares that get you close, then nudge them on the scale until each box hits the mark. Even portions are the difference between a meal plan you can trust and a guessing game.
prose.cost_closing_html: Now the part that matters to your wallet. This whole tray breaks down to ${{cost_ps}} per serving. That is a creamy, cheesy, {{protein}} gram protein dinner for about what the drive-thru value menu costs, except this one is already cooked, already portioned, and waiting in your fridge for the days you would have caved and ordered out. Real food, real protein, and a number you can actually plan a week around.

head.description: High-protein chicken alfredo lasagna meal prep that makes 14 servings at {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein each. Blended cottage cheese and alfredo, breaded chicken, mozzarella, parmesan, and no-boil noodles for a budget dinner.

steps: Preheat your oven to 425 degrees Fahrenheit.
Bake or air fry the frozen breaded chicken breast bites straight from frozen per the package instructions, then roughly chop them into bite size pieces.
Blend the cottage cheese, alfredo sauce, and a pinch of salt and pepper together until smooth.

Assemble: coat the dish with a thin layer of sauce, add three noodle sheets, then more sauce, chicken, parsley, mozzarella, and parmesan. Repeat, using parsley only on the first two layers, and finish the top with mozzarella and parmesan.
Cover and bake for 30 minutes, then uncover and bake another 10 to 15 minutes until the cheese is bubbly and browning around the edges.
Garnish with fresh parsley and grated parmesan, rest at least 5 minutes, then slice and portion into 14 containers.
